text: How many ciprofloxacin studies are there for Escherichai coli?

## Abstract
Escherichia coli (E. coli) is a major bacterial pathogen for which ciprofloxacin resistance presents a significant clinical challenge. To quantify the volume of publicly indexed research datasets specifically addressing ciprofloxacin and E. coli, we queried the NIAID-funded NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE). Using the nde_search_datasets tool with filters “ciprofloxacin” (free-text) and pathogen name “Escherichia coli,” we retrieved one representative record and the total hit count. The query returned 391 datasets in total, indicating substantial research activity on ciprofloxacin in the context of E. coli. This number provides an evidence-based estimate of available datasets for downstream meta-analysis or systematic reviews of ciprofloxacin-related studies in E. coli.

## I. Introduction
Background. Ciprofloxacin, a fluoroquinolone antibiotic, is widely used against Gram-negative pathogens such as Escherichia coli. Rising ciprofloxacin resistance necessitates comprehensive analyses of existing datasets to inform surveillance and therapeutic strategies.  
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.  
Knowledge Gap. The exact number of publicly available datasets focusing on ciprofloxacin and E. coli had not been quantified across repositories indexed by the NDE.  
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: determine the number of datasets in NDE that reference both “ciprofloxacin” and “Escherichia coli.” Hypothesis: NDE contains hundreds of such datasets due to extensive antimicrobial resistance research.

## II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. A single targeted search in the NDE database quantified datasets meeting both keyword and pathogen criteria.  
Materials. NDE database accessed via nde_search_datasets tool.  
Procedures.  
1. Tool: nde_search_datasets  
   • Arguments:  
     – query = "ciprofloxacin"  
     – pathogen = "Escherichia coli"  
     – size = 1 (to acquire count with minimal data transfer)  
     – offset = 0  
2. The tool returns ‘total’, representing all matching Dataset-type records.  
Statistical Analysis. The reported total (391) is directly supplied by NDE as the count of records satisfying the query; no additional calculations or deduplication steps were required.

## III. Results
Data Presentation.  
Table 1. Output summary of NDE query.

| Parameter | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Query string | ciprofloxacin AND @type:"Dataset" AND infectiousAgent.name:"Escherichia coli" |
| Total datasets | 391 |
| Records returned (sample) | 1 |
| Repository example | Figshare |
| Sample dataset title | “Phylogenetic group, ciprofloxacin MICs, efflux activity, PMQR genes, and QRDR mutations among 19 high level ciprofloxacin resistant E. coli strains.” |

Findings. The NDE index contains 391 Dataset-type records that mention ciprofloxacin and list Escherichia coli as the infectious agent.

## IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The presence of 391 datasets indicates a robust body of publicly available data on ciprofloxacin studies involving E. coli. This volume can support meta-analyses of resistance mechanisms, surveillance, and comparative genomics.  
Context. The sample record returned originates from Figshare and focuses on high-level ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli strains, exemplifying the diversity of data sources within NDE (e.g., repositories beyond traditional sequence archives).  
Limitations. The query captures datasets explicitly mentioning “ciprofloxacin” and “Escherichia coli” in indexed metadata; studies lacking these exact terms may be missed. The analysis did not inspect record quality or relevance.  
Conclusion & Future Directions. A total of 391 ciprofloxacin-related E. coli datasets are available in NDE. Future work could categorize these datasets by assay type, resistance phenotype, or repository, and assess temporal trends in data deposition.

## References
[1] NDE. Query: ciprofloxacin AND @type:"Dataset" AND infectiousAgent.name:"Escherichia coli". https://api.data.niaid.nih.gov/v1/query?q=ciprofloxacin+AND+%40type%3A%22Dataset%22+AND+infectiousAgent.name%3A%22Escherichia+coli%22&size=1

## Acknowledgments
We acknowledge the NIAID Data Ecosystem (NDE) for providing access to federated dataset metadata.
